title: India Complete 3-0 Zimbabwe Sweep as Harmanpreet's 91 Seals 92-Run Win
excerpt: Harmanpreet Kaur's unbeaten 91 and Shafali Verma's 69 powered India to 216 for 7 in Raipur, before Nandani Sharma's 3 for 18 closed out the third T20I and the clean sweep.
body:
• India beat Zimbabwe by 92 runs in the third T20I in Raipur on Tuesday to complete a 3-0 series sweep — their biggest-ever winning margin at home in women's T20Is.
  • Harmanpreet Kaur hit an unbeaten 91 off 41 balls and Shafali Verma 69 off 37 as India posted 216 for 7, their joint-third-highest T20I total.
  • Nandani Sharma took 3 for 18 as Zimbabwe, despite Sharne Mayers' 60 and an 82-run stand with Beloved Biza, finished on 124 for 7.
  • The sweep completes the series India had already clinched in the second match — this was the finishing performance, built on an experimental batting order in which captain Smriti Mandhana did not bat at all.

India completed a 3-0 clean sweep of Zimbabwe on Tuesday, winning the third and final T20I in Raipur by 92 runs behind an unbeaten 91 from Harmanpreet Kaur. India had already sealed the series in the second T20I; the third match was about how emphatically they could finish it, and the answer was a total of 216 for 7 — their joint-third-highest in T20Is — and their biggest-ever winning margin at home in the format, according to Cricbuzz.

Shafali sets the platform, Harmanpreet detonates

Captain Smriti Mandhana used the dead rubber to experiment, pushing Anushka Sharma up to open alongside Shafali Verma and holding herself back — in the end, she never batted. Anushka made 28 off 20 before falling to Nomvelo Sibanda. Shafali continued the form that has defined her series, striking six fours and five sixes in a 37-ball 69 and reaching her fifty off 26 balls.

https://x.com/ICC/status/2112608527965671632

Harmanpreet changed the match's ceiling. She was 11 off 12 at one stage before launching her assault, taking 20 runs off Kudzai Chigora's 14th over with two fours and two sixes. She reached fifty off 25 balls and finished unbeaten on 91 off 41, with 10 fours and five sixes — her second-highest T20I score. Her 84-run stand with Shafali carried India past 200 despite a cluster of late wickets, with Beloved Biza the pick of Zimbabwe's bowlers at 3 for 50. India hit 11 of the match's record 15 sixes, taking their calendar-year six count to 128; South Africa, the next best in 2026, have 78.

"Harmanpreet Kaur's unbeaten 91 off 41 balls and Shafali Verma's 69 helped India post a gargantuan 216 for 7 before Nandani Sharma took a three-fer to restrict Zimbabwe to just 124."

— Cricbuzz match report

Zimbabwe fight, Nandani closes

The chase was damaged in the first two overs: Kelis Ndhlovu fell for a golden duck off the first ball, and Modester Mupachikwa followed for 1. Sharne Mayers and Beloved Biza rebuilt with an 82-run third-wicket partnership, Mayers hitting all four of Zimbabwe's sixes in a 49-ball 60 and Biza making 44, but the pair scored at close to a run a ball while the required rate climbed beyond reach. Zimbabwe closed on 124 for 7, as reported by ESPNcricinfo.

Nandani Sharma was India's best bowler with 3 for 18 from four overs, two of her wickets coming in the final over. Niki Prasad, Deepti Sharma, Kranti Gaud and Arundhati Reddy took a wicket each. Harmanpreet was named player of the match.

What the sweep showed

A 3-0 sweep of Zimbabwe was the expected result; the manner of it is the information. India won the deciding match without a run from their captain, promoted a young opener who repaid the move, and still produced one of the largest totals in their T20I history. The batting depth and six-hitting volume — 128 sixes in the calendar year, 50 more than the next team — give Mandhana's side a power base few teams in the women's game can currently match. The sterner tests will come against stronger opposition, but India leave Raipur with a settled top order, a returning-to-peak Harmanpreet, and a young seam attack, led by Nandani, that closed out all three matches.
